verdicts.summary: A prompt that arrives before the dialog mounts is held in the module queue, and the dialog reads the current snapshot when it mounts.
verdicts.scenario: A prompt arrives while the user is on /pair. startSshPasswordPromptQueue (appInit.tsx:136) appends it at line 52. Later __root mounts SshPasswordPromptDialog, and useSyncExternalStore reads promptQueue on its first render, so the prompt shows. Cancel removes the head even when the bridge call fails (line 125). An expired head is dismissed locally (line 135), which shows the next prompt in the queue.

verdicts.summary: The Escape observer now always runs before the _chat layout's window listener, which clears the sidebar selection on Escape. Escape on /pull-requests with threads selected now leaves the page and keeps the selection.
verdicts.scenario: 1. Open /pull-requests (rendered under the _chat layout; ChatRouteGlobalShortcuts mounts because the page is not a modal page). 2. The dispatcher's bubble keydown listener on window is installed once, at the first registerCommands call (dispatcher.ts:88-93). ChatRouteGlobalShortcuts removes and re-adds its own window listener whenever its dependencies change (keybindings load, selectedThreadKeysSize, and others; _chat.tsx:180-196), so it ends up after the dispatcher. 3. Select threads in the sidebar, then press Escape. 4. dispatchKeyDown: no global scope claims Escape and defaultPrevented is false, so consumed is false. The observer at AppSidebarLayout.tsx:180-189 calls preventDefault and history.back(). 5. The _chat listener sees defaultPrevented and returns at _chat.tsx:72, so clearSelection at _chat.tsx:88-90 never runs. Before this commit, the PullRequestsPage listener was removed and re-added on every page render (its handleEscape was a new closure each render), so it usually ran after _chat's listener. Escape then cleared the selection and the page stayed. The new comment says a selection should claim Escape, but the selection handler is not a dispatcher scope, so the observer cannot see it.
verdicts.consequence: With threads selected in the sidebar, Escape on the pull requests page goes back or home, and the selection stays, instead of clearing the selection.

verdicts.summary: The probe runs once in a keepAlive atom. The fallback is replaced only by a non-empty remote-capable result, and a rejection is swallowed.
verdicts.scenario: The probe rejects or returns only editors that cannot open remotely. setSelf is never called, so the atom keeps ['vscode']. keepAlive keeps the probe from running again each time the picker remounts.

verdicts.summary: The open question here (does mounting the shell atoms at app start, before the auth gate, start environment shell streams) is finding 1. Mounting does start runtime stream atoms, but whether that connects before auth depends on followStreamInEnvironment at runtime.
